title: The absolute best time to send email campaigns in 2026
summary: The best time to send email: start Tuesday to Thursday mid-morning, then test. Send-time tips by email type, time zone, and audience.
body_markdown:
- **Start Tuesday through Thursday:** Mid-morning (9 to 11 AM) in your recipient's time zone is a safe first test.
- **Match timing to the email type:** Welcome and abandoned cart emails go out right away. Newsletters do best on a consistent day and time.
- **Avoid the top of the hour:** Scheduling at odd minutes, like :07 or :21, helps you skip mailbox provider traffic jams.
- **Judge tests by clicks:** Apple Mail Privacy Protection inflates opens, so pick winners by clicks and conversions.


## The absolute best time to send email campaigns in 2026


Determining the best time or the best day to send your email marketing campaign is an essential piece of your overall email marketing strategy.


And for good reason.


High-quality content timed to arrive in your recipient's inbox at the right time can help increase both your engagement and delivery rates.


Ever feel like you're shouting into the void when you hit "send" on your email campaigns? You're not alone. Timing is everything in email marketing—it can mean the difference between your message landing with a bang or fizzling out unnoticed.


Although there’s no magic answer to when you should send your email campaigns, there’s a lot in your control to test and find your email send time “sweet spot.”


Whether you use automation or not (we provide tactics for both scenarios below), there is a method that will help you achieve optimal send times. The tips and insights below can help you get started and help you dial-in your send time so your email campaigns have the highest chance of being read.


## Best time to send an email campaign (benchmarks and data)


Wondering where to start? Consider looking at historical data around send times and correlating engagement rates. We pull send data from our senders over holiday time periods here at Twilio SendGrid, and we’ve found that during[Black Friday and Cyber Monday](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/resource/2023-Email-Marketing-Benchmark-Report) , the peak send time across senders was 7 AM, and that peak opens occurred between 8 AM and 9 AM MDT.


And most recently, over the Memorial Day weekend, we saw that the peak send time was also 7 AM. But when it came down to analyzing the most common open times, results varied so much that our data scientists couldn’t find a statistically significant time that people were most likely to open an email.


### What is the best day to send emails?


Outside of specific holiday sending and open data,[HubSpot has also found that](https://blog.hubspot.com/sales/best-time-send-email-report-2015) :


- Sending on a Tuesday vs. other weekdays generally correlates with slightly higher open rates.
- An 11 AM (EST) send time results in higher open rates.
- Open rates tend to drop off later in the week and through the weekend.


So as you can see, not all the datasets will always agree with each other all of the time.


### What is the best time of day to send emails?


Starting with a Tuesday send time at either 7 AM or 11 AM will be solid places to start and use as a control in your email send testing. Again, the best way to determine your optimal send time is to test (and keep testing) variables until you find enough statistical significance to conclude that one time is better than another.


## Variables that determine optimal email send times


Keep in mind all the other variables in place that determine optimal email send times.


For example, those who are in the market to purchase software are probably very unlikely to want to purchase or engage with you over the weekend because they aren’t at work.


But if you email on behalf of a B2C brand, the weekend sends might be some of your highest-converting and engaging campaigns. I know for a fact that the majority of my online shopping occurs on Saturday mornings on the couch over coffee, and I’m often digging through my inbox to find that promotion that I’m looking to use.


## The best time to send types of email campaigns


The best time to send an email campaign will largely depend on your email purpose and your audience. For example, the best time to send an email blast to your entire audience won't be the same as when you send a promotional coupon email to a segment.


Use these as starting points to test, not rules. All times are in the recipient's local time.


Email type Start with Then test Why it works


Newsletters Tuesday, 10 AM Thursday, 10 AM Midweek mornings land after Monday catch-up, and a fixed slot trains readers to expect you


Promotional (B2C) Tuesday–Thursday, 9–11 AM Saturday morning Shoppers browse on work breaks, and many shop on weekend mornings


Promotional (B2B) Tuesday–Wednesday, 9–11 AM 1–3 PM the same days Buyers make decisions during work hours


Holiday and BFCM promos 7 AM on the day The evening before Twilio SendGrid holiday data showed peak sends at 7 AM and peak opens from 8 to 9 AM


Content and marketing emails Wednesday–Thursday, 9 AM–12 PM 7 AM Readers sort their inbox in the morning and save useful reads for later


Email blasts Tuesday–Thursday, 10 AM–2 PM Morning vs. early afternoon Skips Monday overload and Friday wind-down


Event reminders One week and one day before, mid-morning One hour before (virtual events) Reminders close to the event cut no-shows


Re-engagement Tuesday–Thursday, mid-morning Saturday morning (B2C) Lapsed subscribers need your best shot at attention


Welcome emails Right after signup — Interest is highest the moment someone subscribes


Abandoned cart 1–4 hours after the cart is left A follow-up 24 hours later Purchase intent is still fresh


Transactional (receipts, resets, shipping) Immediately — The recipient triggered it and is waiting for it


## **Universal rules:**


- For B2B, avoid Mondays (inbox catch-up) and Fridays (weekend wind-down)


- Send at odd minutes (7, 21, 36 past the hour) to avoid ISP traffic jams


- Test everything—your audience might be different


### Best time to send an email blast


The best time to send an email blast depends on various factors, including your target audience, industry, and the purpose of your email campaign. While there is no universal "one-size-fits-all" answer, here are some general guidelines to consider when determining the best time to send your email blast:


1. **Know Your Audience:** Understand your[target audience's habits and preferences](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/email-marketing-strategies) . Consider factors such as their time zone, typical work hours, and leisure times. A B2B audience might respond differently to email timings compared to a B2C audience.
2. **Experiment with Timing:**[Conduct A/B tests](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/email-testing-walkthrough) to determine which timing resonates best with your audience. Send your email to different segments at various times and days, and analyze the open and click-through rates to identify patterns.
3. **Avoid Busy Times:** Avoid sending emails during peak hours when people are overwhelmed with their inboxes. Mondays and Fridays, for instance, might see higher email volume and lower engagement. Midweek mornings or early afternoons often yield better results.
4. **Consider Time Zones:** If your audience is spread across different time zones, schedule your email to reach them at a reasonable time. You might[segment your list based](https://sendgrid.com/en-us/blog/elevate-email-marketing-social-media-data) on geographical locations to ensure optimal timing.
5. **Device Usage:** Morning and evening times are often popular, as people tend to check emails on their commute or during downtime.
6. **Avoid Holidays and Weekends:** B2B emails usually underperform on weekends and holidays. Retail and other B2C brands can see the opposite, so test before you rule them out.
7. **Industry Trends:** Research your industry's email behavior trends. Some industries, like retail, may see better engagement during weekends and holidays, while others, like professional services, might have higher engagement during weekdays.


### Best time to send promotional emails


Here are some general guidelines and trends to consider when determining the best time to send promotional emails:


1. **Weekdays, Midweek:** Promotional emails often see higher engagement when sent on weekdays, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. These days tend to have lower email volume and higher open rates compared to Mondays and Fridays.
2. **Morning and Early Afternoon:** Aim to send promotional emails during the morning hours (around 9-11 am) or early afternoon (1-3 pm) when people are likely to check their emails during work breaks.
3. **Avoid Early Mornings and Late Evenings:** Sending emails very early in the morning or late at night might result in your emails getting buried in recipients' inboxes or being ignored altogether.
4. **Lunch Breaks:** Sending emails during lunch breaks (12-1 pm) can also be effective, as many people check their emails while taking a break.


### Best time to send marketing emails


Marketing emails cast a wider net than promotional emails. They encompass everything from thought leadership content to product announcements.


**Peak performance window:** Tuesday through Thursday, 9 AM to 12 PM (recipient's local time).


Promotional emails really drive immediate action, but marketing emails often get saved for later reading. This means slightly earlier send times work better—catch people during their morning email review when they're deciding what deserves their attention.


### Best time to send email newsletters


Newsletters are in it for the long haul, not the quick sprint. And that changes everything about timing.


**The sweet spot:** Tuesday at 10 AM consistently wins for newsletters. Monday's inbox chaos has settled, people are in their weekly groove, and they're actually looking forward to catching up on industry insights.


Your subscribers often save these for their dedicated reading time—maybe with their morning coffee or during that post-lunch lull.


Regardless, avoid Mondays (too chaotic) and Fridays (weekend mode activated). Stick with Tuesday-Thursday, lean toward that 10-11 AM window, and focus on **consistency.** Train your audience when to expect you.


## What should you be testing?


To start simple, include a control send time and a variable send time to A/B test your send time. In[Twilio SendGrid’s Marketing Campaigns](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/products/marketing-campaigns) , you can set this up to automatically switch to the winning version after a set amount of time or variance has been reached. For a deeper dive into A/B testing, check out Twilio SendGrid’s[email A/B best practice guide](https://sendgrid.com/resource/email-a-b-testing-and-calls-to-action/#ab-testing-essentials) .


Here are some ideas of what variables you could decide to test first to see what is resonating best:


- Time of day - day vs. evening
- Day of send - week vs. weekend
- Specific time blocks or periods - start of workday vs. end of workday vs. lunch


Once you’ve determined what day and what time of day is working best for you, you can make granular tweaks to try and be the top email in your recipient's inbox.


## When NOT to send email campaigns


Avoid sending at the very top of the hour or 15, 30, or 45 minutes past the hour. Why? Most marketers use these times to send their email campaigns because they come to mind first.


This practice causes a backup at the ISPs which can cause your emails to be deferred. Instead schedule your 11 am emails for 10:55 instead (and don’t forget to observe and record the results!)


Some ISPs have told[SendGrid delivery consultants (Twilio Professional Services)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/professional-services) directly that the ideal time for marketers to send their campaigns is during non-peak times like 7, 21, or 36 minutes past the hour. Sending at these non-peak times will increase how fast your messages are delivered.


## Send time strategy: following the sun


What if your email recipients live around the world, and you don’t have the capabilities or resources to segment out your email list for each time zone to receive their email at the right time? Consider following the sun.


> *Follow the sun campaigns are typically sent to recipients at or around the time that the sun is rising in their geographic location.*


Following the sun gives you a higher probability that your message will be at the top of recipients’ inboxes. This will also reduce the burden on the ISP because the campaign will be split into 38 smaller sends based on time zones (if you have a global audience across all time zones).


Depending on the capabilities of your ESP, you will need to figure out how to tactically send to your audience at the optimal time. Before you can implement this strategy, you will need to know the general geographic location of your recipient.


When it comes to[transactional email](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/marketing-email-vs-transactional-email-whats-difference) , which is typically triggered by an action the recipient has taken, send time can be less critical. This is because transactional email is not sent in bulk to hundreds of thousands of recipients at once, it happens organically. Read more about the[differences between marketing and transactional email.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/marketing-email-vs-transactional-email-whats-difference)


## Frequently asked questions


**Q: Should I send marketing emails on holidays?**


**A:** Holiday sending requires strategy. While major holidays often see lower open rates, the day before or after can be ideal—especially for retail. B2B senders should generally avoid holidays entirely, while B2C senders might benefit from holiday-specific promotions.


**Q: What's the best approach for email automation timing?**


**A:** Welcome emails should deliver instantly, abandoned cart reminders within 1-4 hours, and re-engagement campaigns mid-week during business hours. Consider the user's time zone when possible, and ensure your automation platform supports dynamic send time optimization.


**Q: How should I handle international audiences with different time zones?**


**A:** For global audiences, either segment by geography and schedule accordingly or use the "follow the sun" method mentioned in the article. Another approach is to identify your highest-value regions and prioritize those time zones.


**Q: Does email send timing affect deliverability?**


**A:** Absolutely. Sending during ISP peak times (top of the hour) can cause delivery delays as your messages queue up behind others. Additionally, when subscribers consistently engage with your emails, ISPs view your sending reputation more favorably. Finding times when your audience is most likely to open and interact helps build this positive reputation cycle.


**Q: How frequently should I change my email send times?**


**A:** Don't change send times randomly. Establish a testing cadence—typically 4-6 weeks of consistent testing for each variable—before making decisions. Once you've found a high-performing time slot, stick with it to build subscriber habits, but re-test quarterly as audience behaviors evolve.


**Q: Do mobile users and desktop users have different optimal email times?**


**A:** Yes. Mobile users typically check email throughout the day in short bursts, with early morning (6-8 AM) and evening commute times (5-7 PM) showing strong engagement. Desktop users engage most during business hours, particularly mid-morning and after lunch.


**Q: How do I know if my send time testing is working?**


**A:** Focus on multiple metrics, not just open rates. While opens are important, click-through rates, conversion rates, and revenue per email provide more complete pictures of success. Double-check your test sample sizes are large enough for statistical significance (generally 1,000+ recipients per test variant). Look for consistent patterns over at least 3-4 tests before making permanent changes.


## Start sending at the right time with Twilio SendGrid


Finding the best time to send your email isn't a one-and-done deal—it's an ongoing process of testing, learning, and refining. Remember, while timing is important, it's just one piece of the email marketing puzzle.


Even the most perfectly timed email won't engage your audience if the content doesn't resonate. Always keep in mind the following when determining when to send your email campaigns:


- Start by looking at performance data benchmarks
- Consider the type of email you are sending and the capabilities of your ESP
- Send at “odd” times instead of at the top or bottom of the hour
- Test, test, test!


Remember that email send time is only a piece of your email marketing program.
